Vulnerability Title: The unauthenticated verify-user endpoint is an account existence oracle callable for any email or mobile
Description: verifyUser at src/services/auth.ts:17-28 posts to /verify-user with a caller supplied type of email or mobile and a value - and the endpoint requires no authentication. checkEmailExists and checkPhoneExists at src/helpers/auth.ts:396-478 call it from the registration form and the complete-profile modal on every field blur so the request shape is trivially observable and repeatable. The response distinguishes a registered identifier from an unregistered one: a hit returns success true and the caller marks the field as taken at :412 and :455 while a miss surfaces as an error the service converts into a success false fallback. Nothing in the client rate limits or debounces the probe beyond the field blur. Combined with code review issue 13 the probed value also travels in the URL query string so every probe is recorded in access and proxy logs.
Attack Vector: Any unauthenticated visitor - no account or token required
Preconditions: None - the endpoint is reachable without authentication.
Steps to Reproduce / PoC: 1. POST /api/verify-user with type email and a known registered address and read the response. 2. Repeat with an address that is not registered. 3. Compare the two responses - they differ deterministically. 4. Script the request across a list of addresses or mobile numbers.
Expected (Secure) Behavior: Existence checks are rate limited and return a uniform response so a registered identifier cannot be distinguished from an unregistered one by an unauthenticated caller.
Actual Behavior: The two cases are distinguishable and the probe can be repeated without limit.
Impact: An attacker can confirm which email addresses and mobile numbers hold accounts on the platform - which turns a generic credential-stuffing or phishing list into a targeted one and leaks customer membership. Mobile enumeration is the more sensitive half because the number is also the OTP delivery channel.
Remediation: Rate limit /verify-user per IP and per identifier on the panel and return a uniform response regardless of existence - moving the real check into the registration submission where it is already enforced. If the inline availability hint is worth keeping require a CAPTCHA or a signed token for it. Panel change - coordinate rather than changing the contract unilaterally.

Vulnerability Title: The OTP resend control has no cooldown so codes can be requested as fast as the requests complete
Description: The resend buttons in both OTP flows are gated only by the in-flight loading flag - src/features/auth/components/LoginForm.tsx:214-221 binds isLoading to otp.isResending and ForgotPasswordForm.tsx:149-156 does the same with forgot.isResending. Neither carries a countdown - a disabled window - or an attempt counter so the control re-enables the instant the previous request resolves and can be pressed again immediately. The handlers behind them do not throttle either: handleResendOtp at src/helpers/auth.ts:332-393 clears and re-initialises the reCAPTCHA verifier and sends again with no timing check - and the custom gateway path calls sendForgotOtp at src/features/auth/useForgotPassword.ts:97 with no guard. For the Firebase phone path Firebase applies its own quotas but the custom SMS gateway path is limited only by whatever the panel enforces.
CWE: CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
Attack Vector: Any visitor who can reach the OTP step - which needs only a phone number or an account identifier
Preconditions: The OTP step of either the login or the forgot-password flow.
Steps to Reproduce / PoC: 1. Enter an identifier and reach the OTP step. 2. Press resend and wait for the request to resolve. 3. Press resend again immediately and repeat - observe there is no cooldown and no attempt cap.
Expected (Secure) Behavior: A resend cooldown of some tens of seconds and a cap on resends per identifier per window - enforced on the client for usability and on the panel for security.
Actual Behavior: The control re-enables immediately and resends without limit.
Impact: SMS cost abuse against the platform's gateway and SMS flooding of a chosen number - both driven from an unauthenticated flow. Repeated resends also invalidate and reissue codes which can be used to grief a legitimate customer mid-login.
Remediation: Add a countdown to both resend controls that disables the button for a fixed window and caps resends per identifier - and confirm the panel throttles the send endpoints independently since a client cooldown is a usability control and not a security boundary.
